capitals.name: Bolghar (Bolgar)
capitals.note: Volga Bulgaria page: the capital 'was established at' Bolghar 'Sometime in the late 9th century'; the Bolghar page: 'originally established in the 10th century', 'supposedly the capital of Volga Bulgaria from as early as the 10th century'. The seat before that is not recorded; the Bolghar site is used for the whole early span (low certainty). Coordinates 54 58 44 N, 49 03 23 E from the Bolghar page.

capitals.name: Bilär (Bilyar)
capitals.note: The Bilyar page gives two accounts: capital 'from the 10th century until the early 13th century', or, 'alternatively with the Bulgar city and Nur-Suvar', 'in the 12th and 13th centuries'; the Volga Bulgaria page has the Bulgars move the capital from Bolghar to Bilär under Rus' pressure (the page's words: 'the Volga Bulgars had to move their capital from Bolghar to Bilär') without a year. Used here from the 12th century. The page gives no coordinates: the point is a reading of 'on the left bank of the Small Cheremshan River in Alexeeyevsky District', 150 km from Kazan. Sacked by Batu Khan in 1236.

keyframe_review.note: 4,158 km2 at 44.4-45.4 E, 52.2-53.0 N, 674-681: the gazetteer puts it around Penza, not on the Volga. Kotrag 'began to extend the influence of his Bulgars to the Volga River' and the Volga Bulgaria page places the state 'around the confluence of the Volga and Kama River', so the Volga-Kama shape (Cliopatria 682) is used from 674; no page dates a smaller or different early extent (page silent).

correction.text: the Volga-Kama confluence shape of 682, used from 674 because the page puts the Bulgars on the Volga and gives no earlier boundary

keyframe_review.note: 44,239 km2 (about 41,000 km2 in the gazetteer's cells), 146 of 161 cells in Tatarstan, with Bolghar and Kazan inside it. The infobox gives no area; the page's 'around the confluence of the Volga and Kama River' and 'Commanding the Volga River in its middle course' describe a core of this size or larger, and the Mongol invasion page has survivors settling 'along the Kama river'. A wider country (Bashkiria, Suar) is not on the pages opened. The pages give no change in extent from the 7th century to 1236; the 969 end of Khazar suzerainty is in khazaria's ledger.

43,274 km2: 1,000 km2 less than the 682 shape (northern edge 54.55 N instead of 54.48 N); unverified, no page opened dates or explains the trim. The pages mention 'several raids by other Rus'' in the 11th century with no years.

43,274 km2, identical to the 1072 shape; it runs to 1235, one year before the autumn 1236 sack. The Mongol advance guard of 1223-1224 (Battle of Samara Bend) changed no border on the pages. The Mongol invasion page does record a 1232 step: the Mongols 'subjugated the southeastern part of the Bashkiria' and 'occupied southern portions of Volga Bulgaria' (the page names no city or river and does not say when it ended). The shape is kept whole because occupied land stays the state's own and is drawn hatched from the ledger's occupation_start of 1232 (the part south of 55.5 N, a reading), closed in 1236 when the contest over the whole country opens. The 1229 capture of the upper Ural valley lies outside the shape. Repaired 2026-10-25: the earlier note said the 1229-1232 raids changed no border, which the page contradicts.

ledger.note: 674: Kotrag's Bulgars on the Volga. 'Following the death of his father, he began to extend the influence of his Bulgars to the Volga River'; Kotrag, reign '665 - around 700', 'is remembered as the founder of Volga Bulgaria' in the 7th century. The year is Cliopatria's first shape (674), inside his reign, not a page's. The Volga Bulgaria page gives 'Established: late 9th century' and 'Preceded by Old Great Bulgaria' (destroyed 668 by the Khazars). Cliopatria's 674 pocket (44.4-45.4 E) is not on the Volga; the Volga-Kama shape of 682 is used from the start.

region.text: the Volga-Kama confluence: 'around the confluence of the Volga and Kama River', 'commanding the Volga River in its middle course'

ledger.note: Late 9th century: Volga Bulgaria under Khazar overlordship (mirror of khazaria.json /ledger/12). Infobox: 'Vassals of the Khazars (late 9th century-969)'; body: 'they came under the overlordship of Khazars' and 'were initially under the political and military dominance of the Khazar Khaganate', without a year. 890 is the mid-point of 'late 9th century', the same reading as khazaria's event, so confidence 1 (the page dates the span, not the year). The page gives no Khazar overlordship before the late 9th century, and the infobox gives 'Established: late 9th century' too; the 674 start is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the whole Volga-Kama country, the vassal state itself

ledger.note: 969: Volga Bulgaria ceases to be a Khazar vassal (mirror of khazaria.json /ledger/14). Infobox 'Vassals of the Khazars (late 9th century-969)'; body: the Bulgars 'gradually freed itself from the influence of the Khazars', 'complete independence was reached after Khazaria's destruction and conquest by Sviatoslav in the late 10th century', 'Bulgars no longer paid tribute to it'. The body text never gives 969; the year is the infobox's, and the Sviatoslav campaign it follows is itself dated 'around 965' with a disputed chronology (rus dossier), hence confidence 2.

region.text: the whole Volga-Kama country, the vassal state itself

ledger.note: 1232: the Mongols occupy the south. 'In 1232 the Mongol cavalry subjugated the southeastern part of the Bashkiria' and 'occupied southern portions of Volga Bulgaria' (Mongol invasion page, re-read 2026-10-25; the Volga Bulgaria page is silent on 1229 and 1232). The year is the page's; the extent is not, so the region is a reading (confidence 2). The 1229 step of the same campaign ('defeated Bulgar frontier guards at the Ural River and occupied the upper Ural valley') lies outside the Volga-Kama shape. An occupation, not an annexation: the north stays Bulgar and the page dates the subjugation of the country from 1236. The mongol-empire dossier has no matching occupation_start yet (only the 1236 gain, /ledger/25).

region.text: 'southern portions of Volga Bulgaria': the part of the 1227 shape south of 55.5 N (85 of its 159 cells, about 21,500 km2, Bilyar and Bolghar inside); the page names no city or river for 1232, so the cut is a reading, a polygon because no named region exists

ledger.note: 1236: the occupation of the south is overtaken by the general contest. The page does not say whether the 1232 occupation ended or the Bulgars regained the south before 1236 ('The page doesn't say'); from the autumn of 1236 the whole country, south included, is the contest zone of the next event, so the occupation is closed in the year the contest opens (bridging a silence, confidence 1).

region.text: 'southern portions of Volga Bulgaria': the part of the 1227 shape south of 55.5 N (85 of its 159 cells, about 21,500 km2, Bilyar and Bolghar inside); the page names no city or river for 1232, so the cut is a reading, a polygon because no named region exists

ledger.note: 1236: the Mongols return. 'In 1236, the Mongols returned and in five years had subjugated the whole country' (Volga Bulgaria page); 'In the autumn of 6744 (1236), there came from the countries of the East' ... the Tatars 'sacked the good city of Bolgar' (the Russian annal, Mongol invasion page); Bilyar was 'sacked by the army of Batu Khan' the same year.

region.text: the whole Volga Bulgar country, fought over from the autumn of 1236

ledger.note: 1241: the last resistance ends. The page's 'in five years had subjugated the whole country' is counted from 1236; the Mongol invasion page has the Bulgars rebel 'led by the nobility' after the Mongols turned toward Russia and the Mongols 'then returned and put down the rebellions', without dates.

1241: Volga Bulgaria passes to the Mongols. 'Volga Bulgaria became a part of the Ulus Jochi, later known as the Golden Horde'; infobox result 'Mongol victory', 'Bulgar territories added to Mongol Empire'; the Volga Bulgaria infobox dates the Mongol conquest '1240s'. Cliopatria's last shape is 1235. Survivors moved to the forests, 'the majority settled along the Kama river'.

region.text: the Volga Bulgar country, now Ulus Jochi land

wars.name: Rus' raids on Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In the 11th century, the country was devastated by several raids by other Rus''; the page gives no years and no territorial result.
wars.note: The 985 campaign of Vladimir the Great is in the rus dossier (Vladimir the Great page), not on this page.

wars.name: Yuri II's campaign against Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: 'In 1220, the Grand Duke Yuri II of Vladimir captured Ustiug and besieged the important Bulgar town of Aşlı.' No territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Samara Bend
wars.outcome: The Bulgars ambushed the Mongol advance guard 'in the later 1223 or in 1224'; the Volga Bulgaria page: 'In September 1223 near Samara an advance guard of Genghis Khan's army' entered the country and was defeated. No territorial change.
wars.note: The two pages differ on the date (September 1223 against 'the later 1223 or in 1224').

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Volga Bulgaria
wars.outcome: Mongol victory: Bilyar and Bolghar sacked in 1236, the rebellions put down, the land added to the Ulus Jochi.
wars.note: 1229: 'defeated Bulgar frontier guards at the Ural River and occupied the upper Ural valley'. 1232: the Mongols 'subjugated the southeastern part of the Bashkiria' and 'occupied southern portions of Volga Bulgaria' (the ledger's occupation 1232-1236, south of 55.5 N); the page does not say whether the Bulgars regained that land. The main conquest is 1236-1241 ('in five years had subjugated the whole country', Volga Bulgaria page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the frontier with the Rus' principalities, the Mordvins and the steppe is approximate throughout.

notes:
Page budget 5 (used 5). Cliopatria's start (674) is Kotrag's reign (665 to about 700); the Volga Bulgaria infobox says 'Established: late 9th century' and the Bolghar page 10th century for the city: the 674 start is Cliopatria's, kept at confidence 1. The 674-681 pocket near Penza (4,158 km2) is replaced by the Volga-Kama shape. No page opened dates the conversion to Islam (922, on the Volga Bulgaria page; no territorial effect), the Rus' campaigns of 985, 1088, 1164, 1172, 1183 (the Volga Bulgaria page does not mention them; 985 is in the rus dossier) or the capital's move to Bilär. A gap-filler could open Vladimir-Suzdal and 'Rus'-Bulgar wars' pages for 1164-1183 and the peace of 1220-1221.

End date: 1241 is the page's arithmetic ('In 1236, the Mongols returned and in five years had subjugated the whole country'); Cliopatria's last shape is 1235 and the infobox says '1240s'. If the Mongol Empire dossier has no matching contest over this land for 1236-1241, the contest here will have no partner. The Khazar suzerainty (late 9th century to 969) is recorded here from the repair round of 2026-10-25 (vassal_start 890, vassal_end 969, counterpart khazaria) and mirrors khazaria.json /ledger/12 and /ledger/14.

Counterparts without a dossier: none new; principality-of-vladimir-suzdal, mongol-empire, golden-horde and old-great-bulgaria exist or are written by other groups.

Repair round (2026-10-25, after the adversarial review): (1) added the Khazar vassalage, 890 (confidence 1, the mid-point of the infobox's 'late 9th century') to 969 (confidence 2, the infobox's year), both on the Volga Bulgaria page, re-opened. (2) Added the Mongol occupation of southern Volga Bulgaria, 1232 (confidence 2) to 1236 (confidence 1), on the Mongol invasion page, re-opened: 'occupied southern portions of Volga Bulgaria' is all the page says, so the extent (south of 55.5 N, 85 of 159 cells) is a reading and the end is a bridge over silence; corrected the note of keyframe 3 and of the war. No new page was opened (budget 5, used 5; the two pages were read again). Open for the mongol-empire dossier (ia-02): it has no occupation_start for this land in 1232 and has the gain of Volga Bulgaria in 1236 (/ledger/25), where this dossier has a contest 1236-1241. Not done, left for a gap-filler (beyond the page budget or no page found): a page that dates the foundation on the Volga (Kotrag, already opened, gives only his reign), the extent beyond the Tatarstan core (Bilyar page, already opened, gives none), and the Rus' campaigns of 1088, 1164, 1172, 1183 and the peace of 1220-1221 (Andrey Bogolyubsky page not opened).
